meta.description: Answers to common questions about flight reservations for visas: legality, validity, embassies, names, dates, delivery, refunds and support.

lead: Straight answers about flight reservations for visa applications, including what they cannot do.
body: ## The basics

Q: What is a flight reservation for a visa application?
A: It is an itinerary with a booking reference (PNR) that shows a planned journey. It is a document for showing a travel plan. It is not a paid ticket and you cannot board a plane with it. See [what is a dummy ticket](/blog/what-is-a-dummy-ticket).

Q: Is it the same as a dummy ticket?
A: People use both phrases for the same kind of document. We prefer "flight reservation" because it describes what it is.

Q: Do I pay for the flight?
A: No. You pay for the reservation document only. You never pay for the airfare.
## Legality and acceptance

Q: Is it legal to use one for a visa application?
A: Using an itinerary to show a planned trip is common. What matters is honesty: do not present a reservation as a paid ticket, and never edit a document. Read [is a dummy ticket legal for a visa](/blog/is-a-dummy-ticket-legal-for-a-visa).

Q: Will my embassy accept it?
A: We cannot promise that. Every embassy, consulate and visa centre sets its own rules, and some ask for a paid or refundable ticket. Check the official requirements for your application.

Q: Does a reservation guarantee a visa?
A: No. Visa decisions rest on the whole application: purpose, funds, ties to home and consistency.
## Validity and verification

Q: How long is the reservation valid?
A: The validity window is shown at checkout before you pay. If your decision takes longer, you can order a new reservation.

Q: Can the booking reference be checked?
A: Each itinerary carries a booking reference and flight details. What an airline or officer can see depends on how they look it up. Our guide on [verifying a reservation and PNR](/blog/how-to-verify-a-flight-reservation-pnr) explains the limits.
## Ordering and delivery

Q: How do I order?
A: Enter your trip, choose a plan, pay at checkout and receive the PDF by email. The full process is on the [how it works](/how-it-works) page.

Q: How fast do I receive it?
A: Your itinerary is sent by email after your order is confirmed. The delivery time is shown at checkout.

Q: Do I need an account?
A: No account is needed.

Q: How do I pay?
A: Payment options are shown at checkout. See [pricing](/pricing) for the plans.
## Names, dates and changes

Q: What name should I enter?
A: Enter the name exactly as it appears on the passport, in the same order.

Q: Can I change names or dates after ordering?
A: Contact support with your order reference. If your plans change, you may need a new reservation.

Q: Should I edit the PDF if a detail is wrong?
A: No. Contact support so we can correct it. An edited document can seriously harm an application.
## Refunds and support

Q: Can I get a refund?
A: Refund terms are shown at checkout before you pay. The [refund policy](/refund-policy) page explains how requests are handled.

Q: How do I reach support?
A: Use the [contact page](/contact). We reply by email.
## Which service do I need?

Q: Which page is right for my visa?
A: Start with the page for your destination: [Schengen](/dummy-ticket-for-schengen-visa), [US](/dummy-ticket-for-us-visa), [UK](/dummy-ticket-for-uk-visa) or [Canada](/dummy-ticket-for-canada-visa). For airlines or border checks, see [onward ticket](/onward-ticket).
